text.p: Lescarden Inc said Tuesday its shareholders and unsecured creditors had overwhelmingly backed its reorganization plans, proposed in its Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceeding.
The company said it expected the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York to approve the plan in a hearing expected to be held soon.
The company filed for bankruptcy protection in May 1996. A committee representing unsecured creditors backed the reorganization plan last October.
The reorganization will retire all unsecured debt in exchange for common stock worth $0.40 a share or a market price, whichever is greater.

Lescarden also updated shareholders on the progress in the company's pharmaceutical products. It said Orphan Medical Inc had received Institutional Review Board approval for a human clinical trial of Catrix to begin in May.
Catrix is already licensed by the Food and Drug Administration as an experimental drug for investigative purposes for treating renal cell cancer.
Orphan Medical is Lescarden's licensee for the use of Lescarden's Catrix product as a topical wound healing agent.

Lescarden said it is negotiating with a distributor of food supplements, which already distributes Lescarden's biocartilage material, to introduce Lescarden's Poly-Nag as a food supplement nationally starting in June.
Lescarden said it plans to produce a line of cosmetic products containing Catrix for commercial distribution by the end of 1997.
